text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Your turn for gesture, IRA told: Orangemen's cancellation of volatile parades increases pressure for ceasefire.
- New Nova Scotia premier to review gas deal: MacLellan eyes pipeline tolls.
- ETA slaying enrages Spaniards: Hundreds of thousands protest killing of kidnapped Basque town official.
- Indicted Serb buried as hero: Explosion follows outside UN post.
- St-Catherine Street breathes new life: Montreal's showcase of contradictions mixes rich and poor, old and new, sacred and profane.
- Organ donors' wishes may be wasted: Seeking families' consent leaves transplant patients to die, ethicist says.
- Gold funds rocked by price drop: Bullion hit a 12-year low last week, and some managers fear the worst may not be over.
- Phone firm takes aim at Ma Bell: Already ahead of the pack on convergence, little Amtelecom in rural Ontario is ready to challenge the country's largest phone company.
- Hiring binge boosts spirits: Overlooked spots buoyed by jobs.
- Optimism builds for real estate stocks.
- What's behind Power Corp's European adventure.
- Big is not bad, says merger task force: Ottawa told deals should be judged on individual merits.
- Elan setback adds to jitters among oil stocks.
